Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. We’re seeing an unexpected uptick in traffic for our summarization pipeline and need to add capacity mid-contract. Current plan: +200 GPU-hours / month immediately for the next 6 months, with the intent to either (A) normalize and keep as an ongoing bump or (B) annualize to co-term with our existing January renewal.

Can you share the pricing mixes you support for mid-contract increases? Specifically:
- Pro-rata immediate add-on pricing for the remainder of the quarter (how would invoicing look?)
- A path to annualize the top-up and co-term with our renewal (any credits or discounts applied?)
- Any recommended staged/stepped approach if we want a lower initial commitment then scale in 2-3 steps

Also include attachments if you have a worked example. We’ll need this for our procurement and finance review.

Thanks — Maya

Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we support both immediate pro-rata add-ons and a stepped-to-annualize path. Attached is a short worksheet (pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx) with worked examples; below are the options and trade-offs.

Option 1 — Immediate Add-on (fastest)
- +200 GPU-hours/month added immediately
- Billed pro-rata for the remainder of current billing period, then full monthly rate thereafter
- Discount: standard add-on discount is 10% off list for mid-contract increases
- Invoice timing: next monthly invoice will include the pro-rated charge for the remainder of the current month + the full month if added before the cutoff
- No amendment required for short-term add-ons, but we can capture as an amendment if you want the consumption guaranteed

Option 2 — Stepped Top-up -> Annualize (recommended for predictable budgeting)
- Step A (now): +100 GPU-hours/month for 60 days
- Step B (day 61): +200 GPU-hours/month ongoing; on co-term we annualize to your renewal date
- Discount structure: 12% off list when annualized to co-term; during staged period you receive 8% on the staged portion
- Credit: we can offer a one-month usage credit (applied as invoice credit) if you commit to annualize at the end of the staged period
- Amendment required to reflect the annualized committed quantity and co-term

Other notes:
- We can also offer a capped burst pool for short spikes (no long-term commit) if that helps avoid over-committing.
- Legal will need ~3 business days to prepare the amendment once you confirm the preferred path.

I’m attaching the workbook with sample invoices and the draft amendment language (amendment_draft.docx). Ben — flagging for margin/discount sign-off. Priyom — please confirm billing cadence and whether a single pro-rated invoice is preferable for Flux.

Next step: confirm which option (Immediate Add-On vs Stepped Top-up -> Annualize) you want us to model and we’ll send formal numbers + amendment.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

Ben / Priyom — forwarding FluxHealth thread. They’re leaning to Option 2 (staged -> annualize). I’ve sketched two price points in the workbook: 12% co-term discount (standard for this scale) vs 15% strategic concession (requires our a) approval and b) 1-month credit + extended payment terms). Margin trade-offs below:

- 12% offer: preserves ~22% gross margin; amendment and legal effort standard
- 15% + 1-month credit + Net45: drops margin to ~16% but likely accelerates close and increases total committed ARR by ~24% over 24 months

If we want to push to 15% we should: a) get ADR/RevOps approval, b) include a usage minimum (annualized committed hours >= 2,400) and c) add a short service-level incentive (SLA priority).

Can you each confirm accept/decline on the 15% path? I’d like to keep the negotiation window tight — procurement wants numbers today.

Thanks,
Kim
